incident.title: POST /v1/notify latency spike and 504s
incident.alert: api-gateway: p95 latency on POST /v1/notify above 10s and 504 rate over 15% for 5 minutes.

label.explanation: A template-svc reconciler session opened transaction 99588 on notif-db and left it open holding a row lock on notifications (line 104). Subsequent updates queued behind that lock (lines 115, 117), so template-svc's queries hit their statement timeout and notification-svc's calls to template-svc timed out (lines 111, 112, 126, 127). notification-svc's connection pool to template-svc saturating (lines 134, 139) and the api-gateway 504s (lines 131, 140, 153, 169) are downstream symptoms. The fix is to kill the idle-in-transaction session, not to add capacity.

hypotheses.reasoning: Earliest anomaly is #104: notif-db transaction 99588 from template-svc-reconciler has been open 97s (started around 14:47:20) and still holds a row lock on notifications. After that, template-svc's UPDATE notifications statements hit the 10s statement timeout (#111, #126) and the DB logs lock wait timeouts (#115, #117). Because of that, notification-svc's TemplateClient.render calls time out at 15s (#112, #127), its 50-connection pool to template-svc fills up and checkouts start timing out (#134, #139), and the gateway returns 504s (#131, #140, #153, #169). The contended resource is the row lock held by an idle open transaction. No deploys or config changes appear in the window.

Another way to read it: requests time out because template-svc's DB writes block on locks in notif-db (statement and lock wait timeouts). The mechanism is the same: the reconciler's open transaction blocks writers.
Pool saturation in notification-svc and the gateway 504s are cascade symptoms. They sit downstream of the DB lock contention.

input.recommendedAction: Kill the long-running transaction 99588 held by template-svc-reconciler in notif-db to release the row lock on notifications. Then fix the reconciler so it commits or rolls back promptly: keep transactions short, set a timeout for idle-in-transaction sessions, and don't hold locks across external calls. Consider lowering lock_wait_timeout and the template-svc client timeout so requests fail fast instead of filling notification-svc's connection pool, and alert on transactions that stay active longer than N seconds.
